chunks: Hamza ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alawi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us in Rajab of the year 339 AH. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim informed me in what he wrote to me in the year 307 AH. He said: My father narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Habib al-Sijistani, from Abu Jafar al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said:

In the Torah it is written, among what God, Mighty and Majestic, privately told Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him): O Musa, fear Me in the secret of your affair, and I will protect you from behind your vulnerability. Remember Me in your solitude and in the pleasure of your delights, and I will remember you in your moments of heedlessness. Control your anger toward those I have given you authority over, and I will restrain My anger from you. Conceal the hidden part of My secret in your innermost self, and show courtesy in your public life on My behalf toward My enemy and your enemy among My creation. Do not cause Me to be insulted among them by revealing My concealed secret, lest you associate your enemy and My enemy in insulting Me.

key_terms.التوراة: The Torah, the scripture revealed to Prophet Musa (Moses)
key_terms.المداراة: Diplomacy, courteous dealing with people, a virtue in Islamic ethics
key_terms.مكنون سري: The concealed secret of God, referring to hidden divine knowledge
key_terms.مناجاة: Intimate private conversation (munajat) between God and His prophet

ai.seo_question: What did God say to Prophet Musa in the Torah according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) transmits a passage from the Torah in which God addresses Prophet Musa (AS) with a series of reciprocal commands: fear God privately and He will protect you, remember Him and He will remember you, control your anger and He will withhold His. God also instructs Musa to conceal divine secrets and show diplomatic courtesy toward enemies, warning against publicly revealing sacred knowledge that could be mocked by adversaries.
